findings.text: nested_equations re-implements the nested-jaxpr descent that tests/jaxpr_scans.py:17 subjaxprs already owns, down to the same 'getattr(value, "jaxpr", value)' and tuple/list unwrapping, in a helper module whose docstring states that it 'owns that descent once' so that every structural guard does not write it again; the new guard could compose subjaxprs in three lines instead of being a second descent that will drift from the first.

the post-conditional form mask restates '(saddles | (indices == 0))' instead of reusing the 'retained' mask computed at :3321, so the invariant that slot 0 is always evaluated now lives in two expressions that can drift apart unnoticed.

the compact width is the bare literal 3 in 'compact_capacity = min(3, policy.null_capacity)', with no in-code statement of where 3 comes from; the derivation (measured certificate saddle counts 0, 0, 1, 1, leaving room for a second saddle) exists only in the evidence fragment, so a later reader cannot judge whether the width still fits the states the route admits.

the overflow test asserts that exactly one conditional survives and that its predicate is an unbatched scalar, but no assertion evaluates that predicate on a non-overflow state, so nothing fails if the compaction stops being taken: an always-full predicate (or a retained count taken on the wrong axis) keeps every equivalence test green and moves only the timing table.
